text:
sophie: Quick question — we're evaluating packaging Kerosene-7B into an on-prem installer for a regulated customer. Upstream license = 'no redistribution; non-commercial' and is vague about transformations. If we ship an installer that includes int8 qweights, is that redistribution? cc @liz-legal

parth: If the installer writes weights to disk and the customer can extract them, that's redistribution. Even if it's baked into an image, some licensors view that as distribution.

liz-legal: Correct. High-level: distributing a binary blob (weights) to a third party is redistribution. Quantization probably counts as a derivative. Two paths that might work: (A) get explicit permission/sublicense from upstream for commercial redistribution and derivatives, or (B) deliver a service where weights never become customer-accessible (custodial hosting or sealed runtime). For on-prem that usually means we can't hand over raw files.

aj: From Sales: customer wants an on-prem appliance they manage. They prefer an installer they can run themselves. That makes path B hard unless we offer a managed appliance or a signed/locked image. Timeline: they want something in ~3 weeks.

maria: On the metrics side: native fp16 baseline -> ppl 12.0. int8 prepackaged checkpoint gave ppl 12.7 and spike in long-context hallucination rate (we saw +4% on our summarization suite). We had planned to optimize cold-start by shipping qweights.

tim: Operational options: we can produce a signed, encrypted image that only boots with our TPM attestation and refuses any user-space extraction. That reduces risk but doesn't eliminate legal concerns — if customer can image the disk, some licensors still consider that distribution. Alternative: runtime quantization (on first boot, convert in-memory and delete intermediate artifacts). That keeps no persistent qfile but still writes temp files during init unless we do in-RAM-only.

license-checker: link: https://redwood-internal/model-licenses/kerosene-7b.txt (scan summary: commercial_use=NO, redistribution=PROHIBITED, derivative_rights=AMBIGUOUS)

parth: Implementation-wise, in-RAM quantization is doable: mmap fp16, quantize into process-private memory, then munmap source. That means no qweights on disk. But we must ensure swap and crash-dumps are disabled or encrypted, and clearly log that we do not produce distributable files.

liz-legal: Good notes. Legal requirements if we go the sealed image approach: (1) explicit contract clause that customer cannot extract or redistribute weights, (2) audit rights for Redwood to verify custody controls, (3) attribution text if upstream requires credit. For on-prem installers, upstream sometimes rejects any distribution even under contract. So we should start outreach.

aj: Sales will accept a sealed/manged appliance if we can commit to a non-extractable run. But they'll prefer an option where the customer runs it themselves. I'll flag that the commercial license ask may be required.

maria: For gating: propose these automatic checks before any packaging release: MMLU subset delta < 1.0% relative, long-context hallucination rate delta < 2.5% absolute, and end-to-end cold-start latency < 10s for runtime quant path. If any fail, mark package as manual review.

tim: I'll sketch a secure-install flow and the CLI we must avoid leaking: 
```
# prohibited: repackage/export
rdx installer create --model kerosene-7b --export-checkpoint /tmp/kerosene-q.bin
```
Preferred secure flow (installer builds encrypted image, no exports):
```
rdx installer build-secure --model kerosene-7b --quant runtime --seal --tpm-lock --no-export
```
I'll also add runtime flags: REDWOOD_DISABLE_SWAP and REDWOOD_NO_PERSISTENT_Q.

liz-legal: Start upstream outreach. I'll open ticket LIC-8821 and ping upstream counsel. If they permit redistribution of derivative quantized weights, we need wording that allows commercial use and sublicensing. If not, we must present the sealed image option to the customer and include contractual non-extractability + audit.

sophie: Action items: (1) @aj start commercial permission outreach with customer expectations noted, (2) @liz-legal open LIC-8821 and request explicit derivative consent, (3) @tim prototype in-RAM quant and flags (REDWOOD_NO_PERSISTENT_Q), (4) @maria add the gate tests to the onboarding CI, (5) @parth update packaging docs to forbid export CLI in on-prem paths.

parth: Also propose a telemetry statement we add to customer onboarding so they opt-in to periodic attestation checks (hashes of sealed images) — that might help upstream be comfortable.

liz-legal: We can include attestation + audit language but upstream acceptance varies. Starting outreach now.

license-checker: uploaded license snapshot to LIC-8821.automated

maria: I'll attach the evaluation CSV to the PR for the gating rules. baseline vs int8 csv will be in /repo/evals/kerosene/packaging_int8.csv

sophie: Thanks all. If anyone finds a different upstream release or a permissive clause, please post here. We'll keep this thread as the canonical decision record. :white_check_mark:
